newsitem.title: USA: One dead in copy-cat Heaven's Gate suicide.
newsitem.headline: One dead in copy-cat Heaven's Gate suicide.

text.p: A man whose wife was among the 39 Heaven's Gate suicides in March, killed himself on Tuesday and another was found unconscious in an apparent duplicate of the mass suicide.
"This is being investigated as a homicide until it is determined otherwise, just like in Heaven's Gate," Sgt. Don Crist told reporters at the Holiday Inn hotel in Encinitas, where the men were found.
"The note suggested they were going to be with their leader on the other side of the (Hale-Bopp) comet," said Crist, referring to a note sent to the dead man's daughter.
He identified the dead man as Wayne Marshall Cooke, of Las Vegas, whose wife Susan was among the 39 Heaven's Gate cultists who died in March.
Charles Humphrey of Denver regained consciousness and was being treated at a San Diego hospital, Crist said.

Both appeared to have taken drugs and alcohol -- as the 39 Heaven's Gate suicides did in March -- and one had a plastic bag over his head. Cooke was face-down on the floor in the hotel, just four miles from the rented mansion where the 39 died, Crist said.
They were both wearing black jumpsuits and Nike running shoes and there were purple cloths in the room similar to the shrouds used by the 39 dead in an exclusive home in nearby Rancho Santa Fe.

Crist said police were tipped off by Cooke's daughter, Kelly, who received an overnight package containing a note and a video indicating her father and his friend were coming to the San Diego area to kill themselves.
The woman, who police said was "uncooperative", called Lesley Stahl, of CBS TV's "60 Minutes" and it was Stahl who contacted police.
By tracing the route of the package, police were able to trace the men to the hotel in Encinitas, some 20 miles (32 km) north of San Diego.

The 21 women and 18 men found dead in the mansion on March 26 were between the ages of 20 and 72. They were dressed in similar clothing. They had bags packed and identification in bags at the end of their beds.
Messages they left behind suggested they killed themselves in the belief they would shed their bodies and board a UFO behind the Hale-Bopp comet.
They died by eating drug-laced pudding or applesauce washed down with vodka and then placing plastic bags over their heads.

Crist said the two men found Tuesday had also packed bags of clothing but that only Cooke had a plastic bag on his head. He was face down on the floor, alongside Humphrey. A plastic bag with a hole in it was also found in the room.
"We believe it is a suicide, based on the note the daughter received," said Crist.
Traces of the sleeping drug phenobarbital were found in Humphrey's blood. "It is our belief he ingested phenobarbital and alcohol along with Mr Cooke," Crist said.

CNN television reported earlier that it had received a videotape from the two men in which one of them said he hoped they had not "missed the bus." At the time of their death, the cult members made videotapes in which they expressed their pleasure at going to "a higher level".
Tuesday's suicide was the second time someone had tried to imitate the mass suicide.

On April 1, a 58-year-old recluse was found dead in his home in a remote mountain canyon in northern California after committing suicide and leaving a note indicating he believed he would join the dead Heaven's Gate cult members.
